missionPremise: A wrong FEMA flood determination was being served on an unauthenticated route. GET /api/brokerage/v1/place/node/48021:36521/facets returned HTTP 200 with tier2.flood.floodZone = "AO" and inSpecialFloodHazardArea = true, no API key required. The determination came from a bake that never asks FEMA about the parcel: nodeFacetBakeTier2Cli quantises the parcel centroid onto a 0.005-degree tile and issues one NFHL point query at the TILE CENTRE, then stamps that answer onto every parcel in the tile, a measured median 227 m and maximum 366 m from the parcel it answers for. Lane SS-W11 adjudicated 5,756 disagreements against FEMA NFHL: the flood-hazard-fact atom was right in 5,714 of 5,714 non-split cases and this instrument in zero, including 1,995 parcels told they were outside a Special Flood Hazard Area whose centroid is inside one. Ruled by the operator via the doc_repo planner: tier2.flood and its fema:nfhl-flood-zone provenance retire as a pair, because they are one bake behind one quantiser rather than two stores. Source: _dispatches/2026-08-19_ss-w16_dispatch.md.
completionPredicate: No flood value leaves the node-facets read path on any code path, for any input, to any of its consumers; the refusal is distinguishable from 'no Tier-2 row baked'; a CI control fails on reintroduction and has been observed doing so; and the endpoint continues to serve every other facet unchanged.
completionPredicateStatus: MET IN CODE, NOT MET IN PRODUCTION. See productionStatus.
scopeBasis: The dispatch scoped this narrowly and the narrow scope was independently correct. The brokerage facets route is NOT removed: other consumers depend on it for zoning, land use, acreage and base facts, and an over-broad removal creates its own outage. The cut is made inside the file the dispatch names, at extractTier2Overlay, which is the single point where a Tier-2 flood value enters the API surface. The Tier-2 BAKE is deliberately untouched: its stored rows are the evidence SS-W11 adjudicated against, and enforcement doctrine sequences repoint-consumers-first then retire-the-store. The live fema:nfhl-flood-zone map-layer adapter (brokerageGisLayers, engineSpineMapLayers, planReviewLayerRun, warmingHarness, workspacePreferences) is untouched: it queries FEMA at a real point rather than through the tile quantiser, so it is a different instrument that happens to share an adapter-key string, and retiring it on the string match would be exactly the syntactic reasoning this item exists to remove.

whatChanged.shape: STRIPPED with a typed refusal, not thrown, not 404.
whatChanged.whyThatShape: A throw inside extractTier2Overlay would take down the whole facets response for every node holding a Tier-2 row, including zoning, land use and acreage. That is the over-broad removal the dispatch forbids, reached by a different route. A 404 would tell the card the parcel is not baked, which is false, and would send the web app into its live-fetch fallback for a node that IS baked. The refusal native to this consumption path is a field inside a 200 body.
whatChanged.mechanism: Tier2Overlay.flood is declared as the literal TypeScript type null. A sibling floodDisposition carries a typed refusal. extractTier2Overlay no longer inspects the flood facet to decide whether a caller receives a determination; it branches on the facet's SELF-DECLARED provenance.adapterKey, by exact string equality against a closed const producer set, in a switch whose default assigns to `const unhandled: never`.
whatChanged.whyThatIsNotASecondPresenceGuard: The branch input is an identity (which instrument authored this value), not a shape (does a key exist and is it an object). It is exact equality, never substring containment. It is total: recognised producer, unrecognised producer, absent provenance, missing facet and malformed row all resolve to a refusal, so no input yields a value. And it is exhaustive at COMPILE time: adding a producer without ruling on it fails tsc.
whatChanged.twoIndependentMechanisms: The runtime switch AND the null type. The type holds even if the switch were edited away; the switch holds for producer values the type cannot see. Neither alone is a single point of failure.

t25Rows.predicate: substring containment on a configuration string
t25Rows.cheapestSatisfier: ANY string containing "/property-atoms" anywhere in it, at any position: "/x/property-atoms/y", "https://elsewhere.example/property-atoms-mirror", "./property-atoms.bak"
t25Rows.valid: NO — it selects the route by which a hazard determination is obtained, using string shape
t25Rows.secondDerivationState: 4 — NONE EXISTS, and building one would be the wrong remedy
t25Rows.secondDerivationReasoning: This predicate is not validating a value against reality; it is a route selector. There is no second party who could independently attest that a given base string means the property-atoms BFF, so there is nothing to cross-derive. The remedy is a TYPE fix, not a check: replace the string parameter with a discriminated route selector (a closed union such as {kind:"pe-bff"} | {kind:"cortex-direct"}) and switch exhaustively over it, so the compiler refuses to build until every call site names its route. Enforcement with no trigger that can be missing and no call site that can be absent, which puts it structurally outside both the dormant and starved categories. That is the same mechanism used for the tier2 producer set in this lane's own fix.

Every production call site therefore takes the property-atoms branch, and the else-branch that builds the direct cortex URL is DEAD for every shipped caller. t25Rows.predicate: NONE — the quantised point is used unchecked
t25Rows.cheapestSatisfier: any coordinate within one 0.005-degree tile of the parcel; measured median displacement 227 m, maximum 366 m
t25Rows.valid: NO — it answers for a point that is not the parcel
t25Rows.secondDerivationState: 1 — AVAILABLE NOW, with a caveat that I believe is a defect in the rule rather than in this row. See reasoning.
t25Rows.secondDerivationProposed: the FEMA query point must fall inside the parcel ring
t25Rows.secondDerivationReasoning: Applying the strict two-party test literally: the ring and the centroid both originate in the same parcel record (the TxGIO stratmap parcel fabric), so one party supplies the raw material for both sides, and the row would be filed state 3, internal consistency. I judge that reading wrong, for a reason the rule as worded does not capture. The two inputs are not two fields from one payload. They are (a) the source's ring and (b) OUR OWN lossy transformation of the source's centroid — round to 0.005 degrees, take the tile centre. The transformation is a genuinely non-coordinating second contribution in the only sense that determines catching power: the source cannot produce it, cannot anticipate it, and cannot make it agree. A parcel source that is wrong in every field still cannot make our rounding land inside its own ring. The check is therefore meaning-shaped with respect to the error class that actually caused this incident (our transformation error, 0 correct in 5,714) and presence-shaped with respect to a different error class (a wrong source ring, where the point sits inside the wrong ring and the check passes).
t25Rows.feedbackOnTheRule: The state should be assigned PER ERROR CLASS, not per check. A single state per row hides that one check can be state 1 for one failure mode and state 4 for another, and it hides which failure mode a row is actually protected against. Recommend the column read state plus the error class it covers — this row is '1 (our transformation) + 4 (source geometry)'. Under the current single-state rule this row files as 3 and the strongest available check gets discouraged, which is the opposite of the intent. Corroborating evidence that the axis is wrong: the check that ACTUALLY established this defect was not containment at all, it was adjudication against FEMA NFHL at the true parcel location (SS-W11). FEMA supplies both answers there, so under the strict two-party test that adjudication also reads as state 3 — yet it is what produced the finding.
t25Rows.secondDerivationForTheUncoveredErrorClas: State 2 — AVAILABLE ONCE A NAMED DEPENDENCY LANDS. To catch a wrong source ring, cross-check the parcel geometry against an independent one: the county CAD's own mapped parcel geometry versus the TxGIO statewide fabric. Dependency: a loaded county-CAD geometry source alongside lib/cad-ingest's TxGIO landparcels tables. Not built today. That would be a genuine two-party check.
t25Rows.noteOnEvidencePreservation: Recorded here because retirement destroys the evidence otherwise. The bake code is deliberately left in place by this lane, so the predicate above is still readable at source at the snapshot named.

fourQuestionGate.q4_whatBypassesIt: A NEW read path under a DIFFERENT name serving the same place_layer_snapshots rows. The grep matches a string in ONE named file; it does not match a rename, a second route, or a new service. It is also bypassed by anything that does not pass through CI: a direct push to a branch with checks disabled, an admin merge, or a deploy built from a tree that CI never saw. And it does not reach the Tier-2 bake, which keeps writing the same wrong rows. The grep is a regression tripwire and is reported as such, not as coverage. The semantic guarantee is the type and the exhaustive switch, which travel with the code wherever it is copied.
fourQuestionGate.scopeVersusClaim: The gate claims exactly one thing — on the node-facets read path, in one named file, the flood key may only be assigned the literal null — and its scope is that one file. It deliberately does not reach the live fema:nfhl-flood-zone map-layer adapter, which is a different instrument sharing a string. A control broader than its claim teaches the fleet to reach for the bypass flag.

defectsFoundInMyOwnControlBeforeShipping: The gate was a DEAD GATE, permanently red on a clean tree: the comment-strip regex was anchored on ':LINE:', but rg given a single file argument omits the filename and prints 'LINE:content', so the route's own header documentation matched the gate the header describes. Caught by running the gate against a clean tree and expecting a PASS. This is the exact failure mode ci-coverage-clamp-shared-engine in this same workflow already records in its header, reproduced while implementing the doctrine written against it.

The 'cannot pass on its own absence' guard was SENTINEL-SATISFIABLE: a single probe for flood:\s*null was satisfied by the Tier2Overlay TYPE FIELD alone, so deleting the object-literal assignment read as clean. Now two markers are required and checked separately.

The compliant-file self-test fixture did not match the predicate: the permitted-assignment pattern is end-anchored, so flood: null must sit on its own line, and the fixture inlined it. The fixture was corrected to mirror the real formatting and the constraint documented, rather than un-anchoring the pattern — un-anchoring would swallow 'flood: null, legacy: p.flood', smuggling a value past the gate on the tail of a compliant head.

contradictionsToTheBriefing.briefingClaim: What currently keeps this off Smart Site is baked-facets.ts:430, base.includes("/property-atoms"), a substring test on a config string deciding which of two semantically different flood answers a caller receives.
contradictionsToTheBriefing.verdict: FALSE AS STATED. Verified at hauska-map d3510a6.
contradictionsToTheBriefing.why: PE_FACETS_PROXY_BASE is a compile-time constant containing that substring, so line 430 always takes the property-atoms branch and its else-branch is dead for every shipped caller. It never selects between two flood answers at runtime. Worse, the /api/spine/property-atoms BFF ITSELF calls cortex GET /api/brokerage/v1/place/node/:id/facets, and stripCortexEnvelopeProductTruth (api/_lib/pe-property-atoms.ts) spreads tier2 and nulls ONLY envelope, explicitly preserving tier2.flood, on two response paths that return the cortex body with HTTP 200: the flag-off path and the definitive-empty / adapt-failed path. What actually drops tier2 is mergeBakedBaseFacts, which copies only bakedBody.facets, and only on the atom.ok path.
contradictionsToTheBriefing.theRealGuard: PROPERTY_ATOM_PATH === "1" (an environment variable) AND atomChainIsUsable(chain) for that specific parcel. Both are runtime and data conditions with no test. That is worse than the briefing states, because an env flip or an unwarmed parcel reopens the path.
contradictionsToTheBriefing.measurementHonesty: Code path VERIFIED by reading. A live instance was NOT observed: 13 nodes probed on property-explorer-xi.vercel.app, of which 8 carried a cortex tier2 row, and all 8 also had a usable atom chain so PE took the atom-chain path. That is UNMEASURED, not absent, and it is a parcel sample rather than an area sweep, so it establishes nothing about prevalence.

contradictionsToTheBriefing.verdict: FALSE. PE has LIVE consumers of tier2.flood beyond the inspect card, and two read the anonymous cortex route as their documented contract.
